First, let $f(x)=2\sqrt{x}$ and $g(x)=x.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =g(x) \\ 2\sqrt{x} & =x \\ 4x & ={x}^{2} \\ {x}^{2}-4x & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions are $x=0$ and $x=4.$ So, we need to integrate from $x=0$ to $x=4.$

Now, let's draw our usual vertical arrow through the region to determine the lower and upper functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14264628/assets/71912c1b3d6fbd787a34fa6b5b1829ce0a4e1f6c8e12f25430e18e7c525f5492.png)

  

The vertical arrow 

- *enters* the region through the lower function $y=g(x)=x,$ and

- *leaves* through the upper function $y=f(x)=2\sqrt{x}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{a}^{b}x([\text{upper}]-[\text{lower}])\,\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}x([2\sqrt{x}]-[x])\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}x(2\sqrt{x}-x)\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{4}(2{x}^{3/2}-{x}^{2})\text{d}x \\  & =2\pi {(\frac{4}{5}{x}^{5/2}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{3})|}_{0}^{4} \\  & =2\pi [(\frac{128}{5}-\frac{64}{3})-0] \\  & =\frac{128\pi }{15}\end{aligned}
$$
